description:
Retrieval over the Chaprola code corpus — find worked examples, gotcha notes, and doc sections that match your task. Stitch the top results into your prompt before generating .CS source so your fix tracks real working programs instead of training-time priors.

Four collections live behind one endpoint:
- `apps` (1000) — full app payloads (spec + target.CS + target.DS + format.F + sample.json + source SQL). Default.
- `golden` (25) — hand-picked exemplars covering every Chaprola pattern (P1–P8) and every major SQL feature. High-signal floor; also payload.notes is populated with the gotcha text.
- `notes` (~400) — free-form gotcha text per app. Query on error messages or tricky-construct names.
- `docs` (~80) — sections from COOKBOOK.md, FORMAT_STANDARDS.md, ENDPOINTS.md.

Filter grammar: bare array (any-of), {eq}, {in}, {lte}/{gte}/{between}. Filterable fields per collection: apps + notes + golden have category, bucket, complexity, sql_features, chaprola_patterns; golden adds golden + why_chosen; docs has doc_source, format. Unknown filter keys return 400 with the valid-key list.

Tactic: when writing a new .CS, query `apps` AND `golden`, pin the top 1–2 golden hits regardless of apps ranking. When stuck on a compile error, query `notes` with the error text. When unsure of syntax, query `docs`.

collection.description: Which corpus to query. Default: apps.

filter.description: Optional metadata filter as a JSON string, e.g. '{"complexity":{"lte":4},"sql_features":["window-function"]}'.

k.description: Number of results (1–20, default 5). Values >20 clamp to 20.

query.description: Free-text query (max 4 KB). BM25 tokenisation — Chaprola keywords like 'GROUP BY', 'OPEN PRIMARY', 'MOVE TRIM' work directly.

name: chaprola_rag_search
